_numbering_note: catalog_number pending the base/hybrid renumbering (see gdd-culture-emergence-and-territory.md); csv_id is the authoritative key for now.
sub_palette: near_eastern (egyptian) backbone + classical (latinate) substrate (cross-family fusion, Egyptian-leaning)
homeland: Romkemet (the Nile-province of the Eagle; lit. 'Rome of the Black Land')

blend.backbone: near_eastern (egyptian: the per/nesut/heqa register, the itru/Nile temple-cities, -aa/-et theophoric stems, dj/tj/kh phonology, VSO; the sun-disc cult and the funerary akhu)
blend.overlay: classical (latinate: the civic/legal/military/road register - via, legio, castra, forum, colonia, the imperial eagle and the standing legions over the grain-province)
blend.lean: Egyptian-heavy - the temple of the sun-disc and the Nile register dominate the tongue and the rites; the Latin overlay supplies the apparatus of empire (the legion, the law-court, the paved road, the milestone, the grain-fleet) that governs the Black Land as a province.

_note: NEW cross-family hybrid under the base/hybrid model. BASE_05 (Egyptian, near_eastern) x BASE_06 (Roman, classical). CIV/CLAN DECIDED by inheritance: both parents are Civilized (feudal), so Romkem is Civilized (feudal). Concept: 'Roman Egypt' - the Nile as the grain-province of an empire, the temple of the sun-disc standing under the eagle and the legions. EGYPTIAN-LEAN: Egyptian phonology and the temple/Nile register are dominant; the Latin substrate supplies the civic, legal, military and road vocabulary of the conquering empire (the contact-linguistics pattern: the substrate keeps land/rule/kin/temple/Nile words, the dominant administrative overlay supplies law/road/legion/material words). Common-word lexicon is a SINGLE FUSED TONGUE per gdd-hybrid-conlang-fusion.md - Latin roots adapted to Egyptian triconsonantal shape, -aa/-et endings, dj/tj/kh, VSO. Rank titles: ENGLISH display ladder + Egyptian ruler_native/domain_native (the nesut/heqa register); approved foreign display terms Pharaoh (kingdom) and Imperator (empire). DEITY names are morphs of the Agrippan canon - Egyptian canon-morphs PRIMARY (the abydosian column: Tjuraa<Tulrius etc.), Latinate morphs SECONDARY (the agrippan column), never real gods. All human cultures allow Lawful/Neutral/Chaotic (standard lens).

phonology.palette: Egyptian backbone - dj, tj, kh, h, sh, q; l tends to r; v tends to w; endings -aa/-et; vowels a e i o u (reconstructed); heavy temple/Nile register, VSO clause order - meeting a Latinate overlay: the civic/legal/military stops p t c(=k) b d g, f/s/v, liquids l/r, the -us/-um/-a endings of the conquering register (legio, via, castra, forum). Per the CSV: a balanced rhythm with gutturals (the Egyptian dj/tj/kh over the open Latin syllables); grammar is VSO with case-inflected triconsonantal root-patterns (the Egyptian substrate) carrying adapted Latin civic stems. Theophoric on the Egyptian canon-morphs (Tjuraa-, Oranetj-, Riaret-) with Latinate construct variants (Tulri-, Orlandi-).
phonology.phonotactics: CVC; Egyptian clusters dj/tj/kh and long -aa meeting Latin onset clusters (st, tr, pr, cl) recast to Egyptian shape; stress varies with an Egyptian pull; Per-/Niut-/Ta- construct toponyms over adapted Castr-/Wia- (via) civic elements.

sound_changes: Latin civic-endings drop or recast to Egyptian: final -us>0/-aa, -um>0/-et, -a>-et; nominative -is>0 (legio>regaa, castra>kastjer, forum>peret-mahir core)
Latin liquids and fricatives shift Egyptian: l>r, v>w (via>wat-core/wia, vallum>warem); c=k always
Latin roots recast to Egyptian triconsonantal shape with dj/tj/kh flavor and the long -aa; Egyptian roots kept as-is
Egyptian clause order VSO imposed on all phrasing; Egyptian -aa/-et gender-endings applied to fused roots
retain Egyptian dj/tj/kh and the construct Per-/Niut-/Ta-; retain a Latin signature in the civic/road/legion words so the empire stays audible (the -er/-aa adapted stems)
fusion_rules.source_tilt: rule/kin-line/temple/Nile/land/staple words from Egyptian roots (the Black Land and its sun-cult endure - itru, niut, per, nesut, it); civic/legal/military/road/material words from Latin roots (the empire's apparatus governs - via, legio, castra, forum, colonia, ferrum), every root then run through one Egyptian-shaped sound-law so the split is invisible at the surface

lexicon._note: Single fused tongue derived via phonology.fusion_rules (gdd-hybrid-conlang-fusion.md): Egyptian rule/temple/Nile/land roots + Latin civic/legal/military/road/material roots, all run through one Egyptian-shaped sound-law (l>r, v>w, -aa/-et, dj/tj/kh, VSO); portmanteaus mark the blended institutions of the grain-province and the bloodline. No slashes - one word per concept.

morphology.patronymic_form: the Egyptian register keeps the 'sa' (son of) filiation and theophoric given names; the imperial administrative class adopt a Latinate gens-style cognomen (an adapted nomen carried as an office-name); the throne fuses both - a Nesut who carries a Per- temple-house and a Latinate imperial cognomen.
morphology.compounding_rule: Egyptian construct-chains (Per-[god], Niut-[god], Ta-[land], Pa-[noun]) layered over adapted Latin civic compounds (Kastjer-[name] = castra-of, Wia-[name] = via-of, Koraa-[name] = colony-of): the capital Per-Tjuraa-Wia (temple-of-the-sun on the road), Menkastjer-Resy (the southern legion-fort).

title_ladder.government: feudal (Egyptian temple-and-Nile rule under an imperial Latin apparatus: the Nesut and his heqa-kin at the crown, the sepati-nomarchs over the nomes, the hatia-mayors over the niut-cities; the Latin legate and the legion-prefect garrison the grain-province, the per-netjer sun-priesthood and the scribal house serve beneath)
title_ladder._tiers_note: Egyptian native ladder, ascending, under the imperial Latin overlay. Hatia (mayor) barony; Wer-khaset (great-one of the frontier-land) march; Sepati/Sepat (nomarch/nome) county; Mer-mesha (army-overseer/general) duchy; Heqa-aa (great ruler) principality; Nesut (king) kingdom, shown as Pharaoh in display (the Great-House sovereign of the Black Land); Per-aa (lit. the Great House) empire, shown as Imperator in display (the Eagle-sovereign over the province). The Latin legate (Legatus) and legion-prefect (Praefectus) garrison the grain-province beneath the crown; the per-netjer hem-netjer (sun-priest) and the scribal sesh stand outside the ladder. DISPLAY uses English tiers with two approved foreign sovereign-terms (Pharaoh at the kingdom tier, Imperator at the empire tier); the *_native Egyptian forms are NPC-dialogue only.
title_ladder.heir: Sa-Nesut (king's son / crown prince); Iry-pat (hereditary heir); the imperial heir-designate styled Kaisaraa (adapted Caesar)
title_ladder.display_policy: Ruler/domain titles shown in setting-gen, domain lists and vassal trees are ENGLISH (or an approved commonly-known foreign term where set in 'ruler' - here Pharaoh at the kingdom tier and Imperator at the empire tier). The *_native conlang forms are for NPC DIALOGUE ONLY, never for structural/UI displays.

people_name_convention.order: the Egyptian register carries a theophoric given name + sa- filiation; the imperial administrative class carries a given name + an adopted Latinate cognomen (office/gens); order given-first.
people_name_convention.dual_register: the temple and Nile-folk keep Egyptian theophoric names (X-hotep, X-mose, Mery-X, Sa-X) on the morphed canon-stems; the imperial officials append an adopted Latinate cognomen (Tjuraa-hotep Wareriaa, sun-priest of the Wareria office) over the same morphed stems.
people_name_convention.theophoric: given names built from the morphed deity-names + a common element: Egyptian X-hotep (X-is-content), X-mose (X-is-born), Mery-X (beloved-of-X), Sa-X (son-of-X); Latinate devotional cognomina on the secondary morphs (Tulri-anaa = of-Tulri/Tjuraa). e.g. Tjuraa-hotep, Mery-Oranetj, Sa-Riaret Tulrianaa.

religion._note: Deity-names are morphs of the Agrippan canon - Egyptian canon-morphs PRIMARY (the abydosian column, Tjuraa<Tulrius etc.), Latinate morphs SECONDARY (the agrippan column), never real Egyptian/Roman gods. Standard lens (Lawful/Neutral/Chaotic). Concept: the sun-disc temple-cult of the Black Land endures beneath the imperial eagle; strong funerary cult (akhu) under a Latin civic-religious overlay.
religion.the_one: Atjernaa (< Aeternus; Lat. Aeternaa) - the hidden distant maker, honored not petitioned

sample_deity_renames.Tulrius: Tjuraa (Lat. Tulri) - the sun-disc and right-order
sample_deity_renames.Gaiandus: Geandaa (Lat. Gaiandi) - the enduring earth and the flood-field
sample_deity_renames.Delorum: Djeroraa (Lat. Delori) - lord of the peaceful dead

worship_by_alignment.Lawful: venerates the Lawful powers - Atjernaa the hidden, Tjuraa the just sun, Oranetj of the sworn legion-oath, Riaret the merciful - upholding right-order (maat) and the imperial law alike; names the Chaotic powers as Hefau-kin (serpent-brood) and warded -lemnaa (adapted Latin), set against both the temple and the eagle.
worship_by_alignment.Neutral: the deified dead (akhu) of the god-kings and the genius of the legion-standards and the city-spirits of the per; the great powers invoked at the per-netjer and the forum-shrine situationally.
worship_by_alignment.Chaotic: Venerates the Chaotic powers of the canon, and names the Lawful powers - and Atjernaa - as the tyrant-gods to be defied; the serpent Hefau exalted over the sun-disc.

religion.demon_epithet_pattern: the Chaotic powers, warded as Hefau-kin (the serpent-brood) or -lemnaa (adapted Latin evil), keep their morphs + a portfolio epithet: Maraxus -> Marakhaa the City-Burner (Lat. Maraxaa the Tyrant-Flame); Raptis -> Rapetj the Red Hunter; Vacidus -> Wakedjaa the Devouring Hefau (Lat. Wakidaa the Unmaker).

clergy_ladder.7: Hem-netjer Tepy (first prophet/high priest) / Pontifaa (adapted Pontifex)
clergy_ladder.9: Hem-netjer Aa (great prophet) / Pontifaa Weret (adapted Pontifex Maximus)

religion.religious_orders_pattern: the Per-netjer (god's-house/temple) of [power]: 'the Per-netjer of Tjuraa'; the imperial collegia recast as the Kolegaa of [power]: 'the Kolegaa of Oranetj' (the legion-cult).
religion.saints_pattern: the deified dead (akhu) and god-kings, venerated at tomb-temples as 'the justified [name]' (maa-kheru); the deified imperial founders styled Diwaa [name] (adapted Divus).

holy_symbol_motifs.Tjuraa: the rayed sun-disc above the feather of right-order, set on a legion-standard
holy_symbol_motifs.Oranetj: an iron sword crossed with the eagle-standard
holy_symbol_motifs.Geandaa: the alluvial flood-field beneath the temple-pylon

banks_patterns.military_units: the [god] Division and the imperial legions of the Nile: 'the Division of Oranetj', 'the Regaa of Romkemet' (legion), 'the River-Eagles', 'the Standard of the Sun'
banks_patterns.taverns: 'The [Adjective] [Noun]': 'The Golden Lotus', 'The Eagle and Lotus', 'The Iron Standard'
